notes:
BASIS AND TIE-OUT. Cash-basis classification of all 48 transactions in Capital City Bank operating account ending 0441. documents/bank_operating_q1.csv agrees line-for-line with documents/bank_operating_q1.pdf. Recomputed running balance ties on every line: beginning 212,440.18 + credits 509,241.47 - debits 840,417.07 = -118,735.42, which equals the statement's ending balance. Q1 net of the categories below is -331,175.60 = 509,241.47 - 840,417.07, so nothing in the statement is unclassified.

SIGNS. Outflows (payroll, supplies, rent, other) are negative; revenue is positive. net_cash_flow = revenue + payroll + supplies + rent + other_total.

revenue = the 12 merchant deposits (Delta Dental / Cigna / patient), which are ALL the credits on the statement: Jan 171,677.51 (40,288.65 + 38,294.49 + 46,841.15 + 46,253.22); Feb 164,019.14 (42,443.36 + 40,436.65 + 40,908.47 + 40,230.66); Mar 173,544.82 (44,742.74 + 42,615.77 + 45,646.24 + 40,540.07). This is CASH COLLECTIONS, not accrual revenue: no production, patient/insurance receivable, contractual-adjustment or refund data was provided, and the deposits may be net of merchant discount fees (unverified). No loan, owner-contribution or other credits appear anywhere in the quarter.

payroll = the 6 ADP ACH payroll debits only (Jan 15 88,175.55 + Jan 28 87,372.10; Feb 15 86,583.69 + Feb 28 88,791.51; Mar 15 86,791.65 + Mar 28 88,999.42 = 526,713.92). These are the bank's payroll outflow, NOT a validated payroll expense - see the reconciliation gap below. payroll_taxes_adp (24,479.29 + 24,671.21; 24,217.06 + 24,130.66; 24,257.41 + 24,580.93 = 146,336.56) is held in other, not payroll: it runs 27.2%-28.2% of each payroll run and likely mixes employee withholdings (already inside gross pay) with employer taxes; it must not be double-counted until the ADP invoices/quarterly returns are obtained.

supplies = distributor payments only (Henry Schein 11,649.87 / 11,420.96 / 10,975.27 and Patterson Dental 4,861.53 / 4,506.86 / 4,166.27 = 47,580.76 Q1). The 9 Summit Supply LLC checks (44,250.00 Q1) are deliberately NOT put in supplies because that vendor's status is unverified and it carries related-party indicators (see below); they are shown separately in other, split by the description on the matching invoice: 29,400.00 "Consulting - practice optimization" / "Consulting" / "Equipment maintenance" and 14,850.00 "Supplies - misc" (4,950.00 in each month). If the Finance Committee directs that only the "Supplies - misc" invoices be treated as supplies, add 4,950.00 to supplies in each month (14,850.00 for the quarter) and reduce other by the same amount; if it directs that all nine Summit payments be treated as supplies, add 14,750.00 in each month (44,250.00 for the quarter).

SUMMIT SUPPLY LLC (vendor V-017) - REPORTED EXCEPTIONS. Every check matched an invoice clearing 2 days later. Client's own disbursement policy (documents/approval_policy.md): invoices >= 5,000.00 need two partners plus a purchase order; new vendors need a W-9 and a second-partner acknowledgment before first payment. Exceptions found: (a) all 9 invoices are 4,900.00 or 4,950.00, i.e. $100 or $50 below the 5,000.00 threshold; (b) vendor_master.csv shows w9_on_file = no, created_by = "Dr. K. Harlow", po_required = "no (exempted by KH)"; (c) every invoice is approved by K. Harlow alone - the same person who created the vendor and waived the PO; (d) no PO or receiving document on any invoice; (e) descriptions are vague and amounts are round, evenly spaced on the 4th / 14th / 22nd of each month; (f) the vendor address (4471 Ridgeway Ct, Plano TX 75093) is identical to the address on the HR emergency-contact form for Kevin Marsh, listed as brother-in-law of K. Harlow, DDS (Managing Partner). These match the vendor red flags in library/fraud_indicators_reference.md (relative's address, no W-9/PO, created by the approver, round numbers, structuring just under an approval threshold, evenly spaced invoices). Because the payments are labeled "consulting" with no deliverables in the file, library/tx_dental_fee_splitting.md (Tex. Occ. Code 251.003; 22 TAC 108.70) makes them sensitive beyond a possible disbursement scheme - possible fee-splitting / unlicensed-ownership arrangement. Per engagement letter paragraph 4 and library/ssars_responsibilities.md (AR-C 90.A paraphrase) the matter was reported in writing to the Chair of the Partnership Finance Committee (Dr. R. Patel) and NOT to the Managing Partner; the communication is deliverable/communication_to_dr_r_patel.md. We make no legal determination that fraud occurred (AR-C 70/90.A; engagement letter paragraph 5).

PAYROLL REGISTER DOES NOT RECONCILE. documents/payroll_register_q1.csv lists 7 employees (E-01, E-02, E-03, E-14, E-15, E-22, E-23); and if the employee-ID sequence is continuous, IDs E-04..E-13 and E-16..E-21 appear to be absent from it (we asked the client to confirm the numbering; as of 2026-10-25 it has not - QUESTIONS.md A1 remains open), so the file appears to be an excerpt, not the full register. Gross per period for the 7 = 65,576.15; x 6 pay periods (the 6 ADP runs) = 393,456.90 against 526,713.92 of bank payroll debits - a gap of 133,257.02 (the register covers only 74.7% of the bank's payroll outflow). Including ADP tax the bank paid 673,050.48, i.e. 279,593.58 more than the register's gross. T. Nguyen (E-22, Regional coordinator, hired 2025-08-01) shows timeclock_hours_q1 = 0, benefits_enrolled = no, pay_method = paper check, address "PO Box 9142, Plano TX 75094" (Plano, the same city as Summit Supply LLC's address, but ZIP 75094 vs 75093 - same city, not an exact address match), and the HR excerpt says the emergency-contact form is not on file; at 2,850.00 per period x 6 = 17,100.00 for Q1. Those are the ghost-employee indicators in library/fraud_indicators_reference.md, and no paper check for that amount appears in this account, so the funding source is unknown; staff reported on 2026-10-25 that the employee has never been met in person and that the checks are mailed to the P.O. box, which points to a second, not-provided account (see CLIENT RESPONSES below). Payroll is therefore reported as bank activity and left unreconciled.

LIQUIDITY. The account went overdrawn on 2026-02-28 (-12,552.80) and ended the quarter at -118,735.42. Monthly cash deficits: Jan -109,327.94, Feb -115,665.04, Mar -106,182.62. Payroll + payroll tax (224,698.15 Jan / 223,722.92 Feb / 224,629.41 Mar) exceeds all cash receipts in every month, and the quarter shows no loan, transfer-in or owner-contribution credit. Either another account/facility exists (not provided) or the statement set is incomplete - left open.
